shoal_e04_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_entry.text: On Day Two Hundred Forty-Six, the first thing Yue heard in the yard was an argument over a basket of oranges. Its owner had set it where the restoration lane now began. A clerk moved it toward the public wall, and the owner moved it back. Neither wanted the oranges. They wanted the space beneath them. He Ming stood between the two movements with his hands empty, trying to make them speak before somebody decided an ordinary basket had become an obstruction worth confiscating.

shoal_e04_dispute_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_01.text: The basket belonged to a worker who sold fruit between packing calls. His temporary stall license covered the corner through Day Two Hundred Fifty-Seven. The restoration proposal had drawn a lane across that corner without marking the earlier license. Today was not the day the license expired. The clerk had confused a future rearrangement with a current right to move another person's trade. He replaced the basket himself and apologized in the owner's hearing, not merely to He Ming.

shoal_e04_dispute_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_02.text: The apology did not solve the coming problem. Five packing workers used the corner's adjacent tables, and its short license would soon need a new arrangement. The restoration's forty-housing batch wanted the same dry level surface. A lane map could not give both groups unbroken daytime use without changing the supervised work setup. The packing workers had independent customers and current orders. They were not casual visitors whose inconvenience could be priced as an extra handful of fruit.

shoal_e04_dispute_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_03.text: Yue had accepted a job drawn around this yard. That made her part of the demand for space, even though she had not drawn the offending line. She told the supervisor she would not begin today's comparison until the current stall boundary was restored. He agreed because the existing license made the boundary clear. They performed permitted seated tag work in the meantime. The pause was paid under the accepted reassignment terms, rather than charged to the fruit seller's supposed stubbornness.

shoal_e04_dispute_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_04.text: He Ming brought the packing workers to a public bench when their current order was complete. He represented only those who had asked him to speak. Two others from a different table declined the meeting and sent their own written objection later. Yue resisted the temptation to describe everyone as a displaced group already united around one demand. Shared pressure did not erase differences in customers, hours, bodily mobility, or the amount of uncertainty a household could afford.

shoal_e04_dispute_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_05.text: One packer needed the quay's walk-up customers because she could not carry finished bundles far. Another had a merchant who collected at a set hour and could work elsewhere if that hour remained reliable. A third preferred a quieter room away from the lane's dust. They wanted incompatible conveniences for understandable reasons. Yue could not ask them to vote before they knew which actual rooms, rates, and routes were available. A majority in an imaginary plan would tell her very little.

shoal_e04_dispute_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_06.text: The restoration supervisor had his own limit. He could safely inspect unloaded comparisons before ordinary packing began if equipment was set up and cleared on a new early schedule. He could not hold both tasks on one crowded surface at once. The independent stop needed a clear reach and exit, even for the small applications planned later. A worker brushing past it with a bundle would change the trial condition. Sharing space without sharing hours might be possible; pretending the tasks did not interact was not.

shoal_e04_dispute_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_07.text: Rong proposed paying for a different packing room. The nearest available room was under an inspected ground-floor net shop, entered from the public lane without stairs. Its two ordinary exits were clear, but it stood farther from the quay. A licensed keeper would rent it for a defined eight-day trial. Moving a table could preserve a workshop's dimensions while losing the foot traffic that made it useful. Two packers said they would not accept the move simply because the rent was covered.

shoal_e04_dispute_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_08.text: At the candidate room, Yue watched the first packer measure her route by actual steps. She stopped twice to rest her leg, then said the room itself was sound but the journey did not fit her working day. The keeper accepted her refusal without arguing that a generous offer ought to cure it. A second packer objected because his merchant would not change the collection point. Other workers liked the room's shade. Their choices could differ without making anyone ungrateful.

shoal_e04_dispute_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_09.text: The shared yard alternative required restoration setup before dawn and complete removal of its comparison equipment before the packing hours. Materials would sit under a checked overnight guard rather than crowd the corner. Yue's supervisor would work the same funded scope at altered hours; the change did not buy an additional qualified person. Yue would have to sleep earlier and conduct technical work only if rested. A plan that depended on her enduring fatigue would be rejected before its first shift.

shoal_e04_dispute_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_10.text: The port's new Temporary Space Adjustment Account held thirty-two copper for one eight-day arrangement. Sixteen could rent the lower room, twelve could pay three accepted four-copper moving tasks, and four could carry the notices. Under the shared-yard alternative, the sixteen would instead fund defined overnight guarding while the twelve moved and stored the restoration bench. The four notice copper remained the same. It was a new bounded appropriation, not money stolen from Yue's care reserve or from the displaced workers.

shoal_e04_dispute_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_11.text: Qin explained that the adjustment account could pay the named arrangement after it was accepted. It could not reimburse every customer a packer might lose or declare a refusal unreasonable. No packer had been promised a replacement job. The room keeper's offer had an expiry because another trade wanted those dates. The guard offer had an expiry because its worker was leaving after the eight days. The harbor's practical possibilities were shrinking while the argument tried to become morally complete.

shoal_e04_dispute_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_12.text: Yue asked the workers what an early restoration schedule would cost them. The tables needed to be returned ready, not wet from cleaning or ringed with warning ropes. A packing cart must not wait for a final measurement while the supervisor finished a technical thought. The supervisor could accept a hard end time. Yue would need to stop before it even if a comparison remained unfinished. The whole point of shared hours was that one group's useful work could not quietly eat another's beginning.

shoal_e04_dispute_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_13.text: They marked that end time against the packing customers' actual arrival. The veteran sorter suggested a stop ten minutes earlier than the supervisor's first estimate so storage could clear the lane. He had seen many schedules rely on a last careful worker moving too fast. Yue agreed. The earlier stop reduced the morning's available comparison time. The lost time had to appear in the restoration plan rather than vanish inside a promise that motivated people could somehow do the same amount.

shoal_e04_dispute_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_14.text: Yan inspected the movement route for both alternatives. He refused to let the bench pass beneath an active overhead lift at dawn. Under a revised route, ordinary helpers could move it around the loading zone before the crew began. The extra distance fitted the funded moving tasks if the helpers accepted them. Yue would not carry the heavy frame. She could label its disassembled parts and check the permitted setup afterward, leaving the actual load to the qualified ordinary team.

shoal_e04_dispute_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_15.text: A helper declined the four-copper move because the required time conflicted with her own breakfast trade. Another accepted only if the end time was written. The third wanted to see the frame before deciding. Qin did not fill the names with placeholders and call the crew ready. The supervisor found three actual willing helpers within the posted budget later that afternoon. The declined helper kept her breakfast work and sold them tea without becoming part of the restoration roster.

shoal_e04_dispute_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_16.text: The fruit seller invited Yue to try one orange while they waited. It was sour enough to make her eyes water. He had bought the basket cheaply because the fruit would need sweetening before sale. He was not pretending it was better than it was. She wondered how many of the harbor's bargains relied on people saying plainly what something could not provide. He offered a recipe rather than a discount. Yue bought two from her own money and ate them slowly.

shoal_e04_dispute_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_17.text: In the public lane, Song Mei's venue search had begun to draw comments. Some said an artist should perform wherever offered; others said a port struggling with repairs could not indulge perfect acoustics. Yue had heard neither Song Mei's newest terms nor the keeper's newest offer. She did not add her opinion. At the meeting bench, the packers were making the same kind of decision people called simple when they would not have to live with its hours.

shoal_e04_dispute_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_18.text: By late afternoon, the current license's final date was painted clearly on the corner post. The revised restoration plan showed two concrete alternatives after that date. The packers kept present use through Day Two Hundred Fifty-Seven under either. Today's conflict had begun with an improper movement and become a legitimate future shortage. Correcting the first wrong did not create more dry ground. Yue could acknowledge both without letting the shortage excuse the earlier action.

shoal_e04_dispute_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dispute_19.text: Before the next meeting, she returned to the ordinary routes through which she had met the workers. Her first lodging choice had supplied particular people and particular gaps. Now those invitations could help her test the proposed schedule without turning a paid bed into a mandate. She would complete the promised conversation, then release that arrangement's expectations before accepting another role. The household and courier sources had given her different ways to hear the same impending loss of space.

shoal_e04_lodging_gate.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_lodging_gate.text: The schedule needed checking against people who had offered their own evening hours. Yue gathered the public proposals and left private names out of her copy. Her lodging receipt could explain where an invitation had reached her; it could not authorize her to summon residents or couriers. She went to the meeting she had actually accepted.

shoal_e04_house_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_house_01.text: The night sorter met Yue and He Ming outside the partnership room at the time he had chosen. He said a guard could watch a stored bench, but only if the worker was assigned its location and the key holder remained reachable. A sealed box nobody could identify would become somebody else's problem at the first leak. Yue added a public question about key custody. The sorter authorized the question and declined to have his employer named beside it.

shoal_e04_house_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_house_02.text: He Ming's sister came with a household concern the schedule had missed: early helpers needed to use the public pump without waking residents through a private back lane. The alternative route was longer and fully public. Yue walked it with her while the ordinary carts were parked. They found a turn too tight for the assembled bench, which confirmed why the frame had to be disassembled. A sensible working plan still needed an actual street wide enough to carry it.

shoal_e04_house_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_house_03.text: At the receiving house, the keeper would not provide breakfast before her own stated opening hour. Yue could buy a prepared evening meal for the next morning at its ordinary posted price, or arrange food elsewhere. Hospitality did not add a dawn kitchen shift to someone else's day. The household residents laughed when she nearly apologized for asking. They preferred a question followed by acceptance to a guest silently depending on a service nobody had offered.

shoal_e04_house_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_house_04.text: The anonymous guarding question and the pump route entered the public revised plan. The residents' private comments about which merchant snored stayed out. Yue had fulfilled the night sorter's offered appointment and the household's limited invitation. She would no longer treat this lodging choice as a continuing investigative assignment. If she remained in the room, she would simply remain a paying guest, with new visits or questions requiring new agreement.

shoal_e04_house_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_house_05.text: The courier booking examples were still incomplete from this path. Yue requested only the public definitions through the clerk and received them at the normal desk, without a repeat of the missed commercial meeting. She could ask how a current packing collection was marked, but she had not heard the private examples. The loss of that evening source remained in her understanding. A public question did not retroactively put her at the other table.

shoal_e04_house_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_house_06.text: Before leaving, the sorter asked what she would do if she favored a plan the packers rejected. Yue said her authority extended to whether she could accept the revised restoration schedule, not to moving their property. The harbor would need a separate lawful arrangement with those whose current rights were affected. He seemed satisfied by that smaller answer. She carried the schedule to her supervisor, leaving the household to finish a night that had other uses.

shoal_e04_courier_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_courier_01.text: The booking clerk met Yue at the quay rather than reopening the inn's private conversation. He showed public collection marks for the current packing route with each owner's permitted scope. Moving a room did not move a customer's collection point automatically. One merchant had accepted a lower-lane pickup; another explicitly had not. Yue could see why two workers had rejected the rented-room plan. Their refusals followed actual orders, not a reluctance to be helped.

shoal_e04_courier_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_courier_02.text: One courier offered a cheaper route if the packing bundles were left unattended beside the public gate before dawn. The clerk rejected it because the current owners had not accepted that custody arrangement. Yue remembered how a request mark had looked like a completed dispatch. A cheap route drawn on a page could hide a gap where nobody held responsibility for the goods. She copied the proper pickup boundaries instead of the attractive lower price.

shoal_e04_courier_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_courier_03.text: The inn keeper said an early restoration shift would not require the whole lodging house to wake early. Yue could use the public stair quietly and buy prepared food elsewhere. Breakfast service would begin at its posted hour. A private room gave her control of her own bedtime, not control of the kitchen. She tested the exterior stair in the low light and asked whether the lantern remained staffed during the proposed departure time.

shoal_e04_courier_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_courier_04.text: The keeper's ordinary attendant covered the stated hour under existing inn work. Yue paid the posted rate for her continuing room and kept that arrangement independent of the new space decision. The courier meeting was now complete. She would not treat the old lodging choice as a permanent commercial appointment. If she wanted another private conversation, its owner would have to offer it again, under whatever source limits applied then.

shoal_e04_courier_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_courier_05.text: The night sorter's fuller guarding account had not reached her in person. The public anonymous question was available through He Ming's permitted addition, and she read it without inventing the unshared examples. It identified key custody as a gap. She asked the supervisor to answer that gap in the current schedule. Receiving a later public question did not erase the missed household hour or entitle her to describe the sorter's private working life.

shoal_e04_courier_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_courier_06.text: At the end of the meeting, the clerk asked whether Yue now intended to order the packers into the lower room. She said her decision would concern the restoration schedule she could accept. Others retained their property, current license, and ability to reject a new offer. He nodded and closed the public folder. Commercial access had supplied collection boundaries, not authority over the people whose collections it described. She left with a smaller and more useful map.

shoal_e04_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_rejoin_01.text: On Day Two Hundred Fifty-Two, a gust lifted the edge of the corner's tarred cover. Rainwater fell across a packing table and blurred two private collection slips. The owners moved their bundles first, then agreed to have the relevant clerk reconstruct those requests from retained records. Yue held the ordinary door open while people carried dry goods through it. No one needed her to save the ink magically. They needed a clear route and the right clerk's actual copy.

shoal_e04_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_rejoin_02.text: The storm made the space conflict feel urgent without changing its authority. The current stall license still ran through the fifty-seventh day. The proposed eight-day adjustment would begin on Day Two Hundred Fifty-Eight and end on Two Hundred Sixty-Five. All later space use would need a new arrangement. He Ming refused a merchant's suggestion that anyone who accepted the trial had agreed to whatever the harbor chose afterward. A trial date was not a permanent surrender.

shoal_e04_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_rejoin_03.text: The supervisor laid out what Yue's part could change. She could accept the earlier bounded schedule and smaller likely comparison output, preserving daytime packing under renewed temporary permission. Or she could keep daytime restoration at the original pace while a separately offered lower room served only workers who accepted it. The two unwilling movers would retain their right to refuse, but their old corner license would expire. Neither arrangement could create a second dry yard or promise later orders.

shoal_e04_space_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_space_choice.text: Yue could accept dawn restoration work for the eight-day trial, with a hard stop before packing and fewer comparisons completed during the term. The adjusted account would pay storage guarding and bench moves. Or she could keep the full daytime comparison schedule while three willing packers took the paid lower room; two others refused that move and would lose their old corner when its temporary license expired. She chose which restoration schedule she could responsibly work.

choices.text: Accept the dawn schedule and leave the daytime corner to packing.
Keep daytime restoration and support the willing lower-room move.

shoal_e04_dawn_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_01.text: The supervisor accepted Yue's revised hours only after she demonstrated a realistic rest plan without increasing anyone else's unpaid work. She would end evenings early, buy prepared food at ordinary rates, and report fatigue before a technical setup. His own paid scope shifted rather than doubled. The harder part was the output plan. Eight housings likely to fit the original sequence now stayed marked pending for a later separately funded worker. Yue signed that reduction beside the accepted schedule.

shoal_e04_dawn_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_02.text: Three ordinary helpers inspected the disassembled bench and accepted their four-copper moving tasks. The guard accepted sixteen copper for the eight specified nights, with the storage location, keys, and reachable supervisor named. Four copper paid the actual notice dispatch. None of these workers had to agree to a future term to receive this one. The packing workers accepted the renewed daytime corner for the same eight-day trial, retaining their own orders and wages.

shoal_e04_dawn_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_03.text: Before dawn on the first trial day, Yue found the helpers drinking tea beside the route Yan had approved. She did not join the heavy lift. She checked part labels and waited while the frame passed around the active loading zone. One helper stopped to reset a slipping handhold, and the others waited. Their end time remained paid under the accepted moving scope. A tight schedule that punished a safe stop would destroy the very arrangement it was supposed to make possible.

shoal_e04_dawn_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_04.text: The comparison setup finished later than the first estimate. The supervisor shortened the permitted work window instead of asking packers to postpone their customers. Yue completed one less observation than planned, then stopped at the marked time. The equipment was disassembled and stored before the first packing cart arrived. A packer ran her hand over the dry table and found no grit. She said it would do. That modest approval felt more solid than praise for sacrifice.

shoal_e04_dawn_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_05.text: Rong visited at his usual hour and found the technical bench already gone. He would need the earlier appointment if he wanted to observe permitted results. He disliked it and changed his route for the next day. The supplier's convenience had moved too; Yue could not describe the choice as costing only her own sleep. The eight pending housings now appeared on the revised delivery estimate, where a customer could actually see the missing completed work.

shoal_e04_dawn_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_06.text: The fruit seller used his renewed corner license but declined to sell breakfast before dawn. The helpers bought prepared tea elsewhere. He Ming said the shared-yard arrangement had preserved the workers' daytime contact with customers, not made them indebted to Yue. She agreed and asked him to correct anyone who called the new hours a favor to the poor. These were working people accepting a narrow public arrangement, not characters waiting to reward her goodness.

shoal_e04_dawn_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_07.text: By the third early morning, Yue was more tired than her planned rest should have allowed. She reported the condition before a comparison. The supervisor kept her on ordinary seated tags and referred the persistent shoulder discomfort for qualified assessment if it failed to settle. The pay followed the actual permitted shift. The reduced output plan took another adjustment within its pending allowance. She could honor the shared-space agreement without pretending that a noble schedule made fatigue harmless.

shoal_e04_dawn_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_08.text: That evening, a child at the corner asked why the equipment disappeared every day. The packer said the yard belonged to different work at different times under the current terms. Yue nearly added an explanation of the stop cover and decided the child had not asked for it. He wanted to know whether his mother's table would be there tomorrow. She could answer that for the accepted trial dates. Beyond them, adults still had a meeting to finish.

shoal_e04_dawn_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_09.text: The two packers who had refused the lower room continued their own corner collections. Their customers stayed within the existing routes, and no refusal cost them access during the trial. Three others still wished the shade of the room had been available alongside the corner. They could not use the adjustment purse twice. He Ming helped them seek future options without claiming Yue had resolved every difference. Preserving a shared surface did not erase the reasons people wanted separate ones.

shoal_e04_dawn_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_10.text: On Day Two Hundred Sixty-One, Rong asked whether an extended private session could use the afternoon after packing ended. The supervisor refused under the current licensed and funded setup. Yue's rest plan and the hard clearance time did not leave an unpriced second shift. A useful pending answer stayed pending. Rong accepted the refusal after some angry arithmetic. The missing observations were an actual cost of this choice, not a temporary suspense that would later vanish because everyone meant well.

shoal_e04_dawn_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_11.text: The guard reported a minor leak above the storage area and moved the boxed equipment only within the named dry alternative, calling the supervisor as agreed. Nothing was lost. The repair belonged to the keeper's current ordinary maintenance terms. Yue checked the resulting location before the next setup and learned why the anonymous key-custody question had mattered. A workable schedule included someone able to act when she was asleep, without guessing what ownership allowed.

shoal_e04_dawn_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_dawn_12.text: As the trial approached its last day, the packing workers prepared a separate proposal for later corner use. Yue did not sign as their delegate. Her dawn schedule would end on the defined date, after which the remaining restoration shifts would follow their accepted revised task list. Thirty paid shifts still required actual work; the comparison tally would remain smaller. The corner's preserved orders and the eight pending housings would both survive in the final account.

shoal_e04_room_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_01.text: Yue kept the original daytime restoration schedule after the supervisor confirmed that its physical setup remained safe. The adjustment account paid sixteen copper for the inspected ground-floor room's eight-day rent, twelve for three accepted four-copper moving tasks, and four for actual notices. Only three willing packers accepted that room. Its sound exits and paid rate did not override the two other workers' reasons for refusing. Their corner license would still expire on its stated date.

shoal_e04_room_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_02.text: The three movers inventoried their own tables and goods before the ordinary helpers touched them. One worker kept a private customer ledger in her own bag rather than putting it with the furniture. The room keeper received the tables, not rights to the packing business. Yue helped read the public route marks while the accepted movers directed their property. She was not their employer, and the restoration grant did not acquire their future work merely because its schedule had displaced them.

shoal_e04_room_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_03.text: At the old corner, the fruit seller packed his unsold oranges after the current license ended. He declined the lower room because its quieter lane would not bring passing customers. A packing worker with a difficult leg accepted a separate short route for her existing merchant but refused to say it was as good as the corner. Han recorded only the new arrangements they actually accepted. Refusal left a practical hole in their livelihood that a tidy relocation diagram could not close.

shoal_e04_room_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_04.text: Yue returned to the daytime bench and found the uninterrupted schedule productive. The supervisor could maintain one setup through the funded window instead of clearing it for another trade. The forty housings all remained within the planned observation sequence, with no guarantee that every part would pass. More completed comparisons would help owners make decisions. The benefit was real, and so was the corner's emptiness when its former customers arrived looking for the people they had known.

shoal_e04_room_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_05.text: One customer found the public notice and walked to the lower room. Another refused the longer route and canceled a small order under his own terms. The willing movers had not been promised that every customer would follow. He Ming asked the supplier group to fund future collection help; the group postponed its decision. Yue could support his public request but could not turn the current four-copper notice budget into an unfunded courier service until agreement appeared.

shoal_e04_room_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_06.text: At the lower room, the shaded work surface kept packing cloth cleaner than the yard had. A worker who had favored the move said so without being asked to approve the whole policy. The keeper enforced the room's posted closing hour because another licensed trade used it after the trial. Comfort had improved while foot traffic had worsened. Their experience would not fit a single verdict that Yue could quote as proof that choosing daytime restoration had been right.

shoal_e04_room_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_07.text: The fruit seller tried a public market stall for one afternoon and paid its actual small fee himself. He sold fewer oranges and went home with a sour joke about how fruit had become too expensive to be charitable. Yue bought two at the posted rate when she passed, but she did not become a replacement market. Buying everything to erase the loss would have changed the trade into dependence on her purse rather than restoring its customers.

shoal_e04_room_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_08.text: During the uninterrupted comparison hours, Rong could attend at the ordinary daytime appointment. He saw the pending delivery questions narrow as more housings reached unloaded observation. He called the schedule sensible. Yue said the packing relocation had costs outside his delivery list. Rong agreed to read the workers' next public proposal without promising a payment he had not obtained. His satisfaction and their losses could coexist; one did not reveal the other to be imaginary.

shoal_e04_room_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_09.text: One of the two workers who refused the room found a short packing contract at a different quay. The other chose to finish her current orders from an accepted household workbench while seeking a closer licensed surface. She did not authorize Yue to publish that household's address. The missed walk-up commissions remained missed. A new small contract helped someone continue; it did not make a displaced group whole or prove that everyone who refused assistance could easily replace it.

shoal_e04_room_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_10.text: Yue met He Ming outside the lower room after work. He was angry at the harbor's failure to offer a longer-term space before reallocating the corner. He was less angry at Yue than she expected, because she had never promised to command the harbor's land. Still, he wanted her public support for a later arrangement and did not invite her to celebrate the comparison tally. She accepted both boundaries. A relationship could become more demanding without turning into a numerical punishment.

shoal_e04_room_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_11.text: The room keeper and workers reviewed the eighth-day exit condition before it became urgent. Tables would be removed under their accepted moving arrangement, and no private papers would remain. Any later tenancy required a new offer. Yue's restoration would continue within its own term after the trial ended. The workers' search for space would continue too. A temporary room had given three people actual workdays; it had not purchased their consent to permanent displacement.

shoal_e04_room_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_room_12.text: By the end of the trial, the full forty-housing observation sequence remained feasible within the restoration term, subject to current source limits and qualified rejection. The three willing movers kept the work they had actually performed. The other two kept their refusals and the routes they had found themselves. Lost corner commissions were absent from every restoration success column. Yue asked Han to retain the public displacement note beside the final batch tally, where a later reader could see the cost.

shoal_e04_after_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_after_01.text: The eight-day space trial ended on Day Two Hundred Sixty-Five. Its chosen arrangement had produced actual work and actual losses, while the restoration term still had its final accepted shifts ahead. Beyond the yard, the surviving material from the earlier single-crate retrieval had reached a different owner's decision. Yue visited only the place that had offered her a current invitation.

shoal_e04_print_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_print_01.text: The maker's daughter invited Yue to see the dried readable blocks. Eight carried usable letters and tide marks; four carried comic fish. The three doubtful pieces still required assessment, and the five unidentifiable damaged surfaces remained lost. She had spoken with her brother and decided to permit school copying of the eight educational faces. The originals remained hers. The fish and dedication were not part of this permission, whatever a public clerk might have hoped.

shoal_e04_print_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_print_02.text: The school accepted the limited copying offer rather than announcing a recovered gift of the whole crate. Its ordinary print worker made one trial sheet under the owner's current supervision. A reversed letter appeared at the edge because the worker had set one block incorrectly, not because the wood held a hidden message. They corrected the setup and preserved the imperfect sheet as an ordinary workshop example. Yue enjoyed the fish most precisely because she was not allowed to publish them.

shoal_e04_print_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_print_03.text: Song Mei arrived to discuss an offered later reading of the permitted school sheet. She wanted the daughter's separate agreement to any family anecdote and would not treat the educational permission as story rights. The daughter accepted a brief account of the retrieved letters and declined her father's quarrel with the tax official. Yue listened while two living women set the scope. Saving an object had opened this encounter, but Yue was neither its owner nor its editor.

shoal_e04_print_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_print_04.text: The clinic's original sleeve session remained canceled. Its replacement order now had a proposed later delivery, dependent on its own supplier and fuel schedule. The keeper sent a plain update to Yue because she had chosen the other retrieval. She kept it beside the school invitation. The permitted copied letters were a real gain, and the missed maintenance remained a real loss. One current owner could approve an event without forgiving or canceling another owner's delayed work.

shoal_e04_clinic_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_clinic_01.text: The clinic held its permitted maintenance session on Day Two Hundred Sixty-Three using the twelve surviving sleeves that had passed unloaded fitting. Qualified ordinary staff controlled its lamps and fuel. Yue observed from the public waiting side by invitation and did not supply energy or authorize treatment. The renewed lamps supported the clinic's existing posted hours. No extra practitioner appeared because the glass fitted, and no patient was promised recovery by the restoration worker who had helped sort it.

shoal_e04_clinic_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_clinic_02.text: A rejected sleeve with the scratched flower remained in the owner's closed waste container pending proper disposal. The keeper invited its former attendant to see the mark before disposal, but she declined because she no longer lived nearby. He retained only the offer and her refusal, not a sentimental reunion invented for visitors. Objects could carry memory without obliging their former users to return. Yue found the refusal more affecting than an arranged scene of gratitude would have been.

shoal_e04_clinic_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_clinic_03.text: The maker's daughter had declined the school's proposed imagined replacement blocks. She chose to tell her brother about the loss privately. Song Mei had walked with her and now sought a separate performance room, without turning that conversation into a public lament. Yue received no invitation to the family's discussion. The clinic's working lamps did not make that absence a punishment. It showed where the chosen retrieval had preserved a technical opportunity and lost an artistic one.

shoal_e04_clinic_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_clinic_04.text: At the clinic door, the keeper thanked Yue for the parts and asked her not to repeat a rumor that cultivation had restored the cracked glass. She agreed and corrected the rumor in the public room when it appeared. Twelve sleeves had survived and passed ordinary fitting; the others had not. The printing originals remained irretrievably dispersed. A truthful account could honor the maintenance work without finding a miracle in the particular loss that made its rescue possible.

shoal_e04_close_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_close_01.text: Across the five completed working weeks, Yue had performed twenty-five accepted shifts and received five twenty-five-copper settlements, one hundred twenty-five in all. The final five shifts remained scheduled within the original six-week term. The new space account paid only the chosen named eight-day arrangement. Han closed that narrow adjustment without declaring the packing trade's future solved. A worker carrying his own table past the room asked when the next space meeting would actually happen.

shoal_e04_close_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_close_02.text: He Ming posted the meeting request with the workers' permitted names. It asked for a later ordinary license arrangement and a reply date, not a permanent right manufactured from an expired trial. The harbor's land office would answer under its own process. Yue offered her public observations about the shared route and left the group to choose its representatives. They had work to do after she returned to the restoration batch, whether she felt hopeful about it or not.

shoal_e04_close_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_close_03.text: Near the public wall, the fruit seller scraped a bad orange into a bucket. A child wanted to know whether all oranges tasted that bitter. He gave her a piece of a sound one and charged her mother's ordinary price. His business had not become a symbol he must perform perfectly for Yue. He could be irritated, generous, and worried about his next space at once. She bought thread at the neighboring stall and let both trades continue.

shoal_e04_close_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_close_04.text: Song Mei's new public notice named an inspected room and a performance for the evening of Day Two Hundred Sixty-Five. It stated a fixed audience capacity and a separate price for permitted sheets. The room keeper's share was now bounded, and Song Mei retained her own script and unoffered stories. The notice invited attendance. It did not invite the harbor to recast the artist as its grateful chronicler. Yue wanted to go for the voice she had missed.

shoal_e04_close_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_close_05.text: She checked that the performance would begin after the space trial's final clearing and before her own needed sleep. Her next technical shift was not scheduled until Day Two Hundred Sixty-Seven. Tomorrow's carried-property duties would follow the actual incoming terms, if any remained. She could buy a ticket from her own settled wage without charging an interview grant already closed. A little pleasure deserved the same honest funding as a practical task.

shoal_e04_exit.speaker: narrator
shoal_e04_exit.text: At the door, an attendant asked whether she wanted the public bench or a separate stool. Yue chose the bench, hoping to hear the audience as well as the performer tonight.
